allow.description: Extra hosts the sandbox may reach in limited mode.

packageManagers.description: Allows the package managers' registries in limited mode.

name.description: Unique name per kind. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.

labels.description: Labels for selecting resources, for example from a Target's agents.selector.

annotations.description: Notes about how the resource is operated rather than what it is, such as an agent's owner, trigger or target autonomy. Keys are like label keys; values are any text. They're never part of a digest or sent to a host, so changing one changes nothing deployed. solaria status -o json shows an agent's.

go.description: Go modules, installed with go install.

packages.description: Packages to install, by package manager, in each manager's own pin syntax.

network.description: Outbound network access. When omitted, access is limited to the hosts the agents need.

resources.description: Memory and disk caps, where the placement allows them.

image.description: Replaces the generated sandbox image: a container image reference, or a path to a Dockerfile relative to this file. Only container placements accept it.

isolation.description: Wraps each run in an OS-level sandbox, on placements that don't have one of their own. srt runs the process placement's launcher inside Anthropic's sandbox-runtime, which must be installed: writes are limited to the run's scratch folders and the inputs the agent may write, and the network to the hosts the agents need. macOS and Linux only.

SandboxSpec.description: Describes a sandbox in a form every placement understands.

metadata.description: Identifies the Environment. The name default is reserved for the built-in sandbox.

title: Solaria Environment
description: A reusable sandbox: the packages, network, resources and isolation an agent's tools run with. Targets assign Environments to their agents, and the target's placement decides how one is built: an image for docker, srt settings for process, a Managed Agents environment for managed-agents. It isn't part of any agent's digest.
